title: TRINITY ESALC-I GVPT2 and IR with GDV fixed-frame stencil
summary: Use a common reference Eckart frame and the GDV 0.01 angstrom sqrt(amu) single-mode displacement for Hessian and property-derivative acquisition.
gates: Frozen SMITH definition and ESALC-I chart have the same full-rank Wilson row space
Sparse B prime has no numerical fallback primitives at any stencil point
Fixed SMITH-to-ESALC-I row transform and Cartesian angstrom-to-bohr derivative conversion
Complete vibrational G double-prime from single-mode differences of analytic Wilson G prime
Only reference and plus/minus single-mode Cartesian Hessians and dipole samples
Fermi-only resonance polyads and second-order IR transition moments
Automatic mass-weighted Eckart alignment at every displaced ESALC-I geometry
Harmonic ESALC-I/ESALC-C frequencies and IR intensities from the same Cartesian Hessian and dipole Jacobian agree within numerical tolerance
Provider transports every returned Cartesian derivative into the reference frame and certifies coherent integration grids across the stencil
Every mode uses 0.01 angstrom sqrt(amu); the dimensionless displacement follows its harmonic frequency
Electronic-point cache identity separates symmetry-following tensor transport from legacy points
Equivalent Hessian displacement directions are averaged for cubic constants; energy and gradient estimators remain diagnostics
coordinate_policy: Orient the reference geometry once in its Eckart frame. Keep that Cartesian frame for all single-mode displacements; use the 0.01 angstrom sqrt(amu) mass-weighted step for every mode.
backend_policy: KeyMaker requires a fixed_cartesian_frame declaration backed by coherent electronic integration grids; rotating separately computed Gaussian Hessians into one Cartesian frame is insufficient for a small-step fourth derivative.
